items.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: I’ve been overseas another time with Slam Stewart, Johnny Guarnieri, Pat Flowers and we did a tribute to Fats, it was called a “Tribute to Fats Waller.”

ctx.x: Well it’s funny that you’re not the first person I’ve talked to that may not have the records that they played on. Now to me, I say boy I want every record I played on.

That’s true, what you’re saying. Now that record, it’s hard to get. It’s on Odyssey label. And I’ve been overseas another time with Slam Stewart, Johnny Guarnieri, Pat Flowers and we did a tribute to Fats, it was called a “Tribute to Fats Waller.” And oh we recorded a lot of wonderful tunes. And some of the stuff that was recorded on Black & Blue, and Slam did some things with Johnny, who he had worked with quite a bit long before, you know with Prez and all those other guys. And so when we recorded that I got a…
And when you look at some of these great artists like Milt Hinton and so forth — it must be such a thrill to play—

items.title: 67849_Leroy Elliot Stewart oral history interview
items.q: Joe Marshall on drums, you know, and of course, I mentioned before, Johnny Guarnieri on piano, Jimmy Shirley on guitar and Jackie Williams on drums.

ctx.x: Joe Marshall on drums, you know, and of course, I mentioned before, Johnny Guarnieri on piano, Jimmy Shirley on guitar and Jackie Williams on drums.
So those were the groups that you recorded with when you were there.
